title: Jira Issues
author: Atlas core
description: Create, read, update, transition, comment on, assign or search Atlassian Jira issues through a server-registered instance. The operation and its values are authored in the model; the site URL and the credential live on the server, resolved from the vault (ADR-0201). A transition may be named by the button Jira shows — its id is resolved first — and a search follows Jira's paging to the authored maximum.

properties.label: Connector
properties.description: Name of the server-registered Jira instance (Console → Connectors), never a URL.

properties.label: Issue (read/update/transition/comment/assign)
properties.description: Issue key (OPS-42) or numeric id. Usually a FEEL expression naming what an earlier Create issue wrote, e.g. =ticket.key.

properties.label: Project (create)
properties.description: Project key. A value that is all digits is read as a project id instead.

properties.label: Issue type (create)
properties.description: Issue type by the name Jira shows (Task, Bug, Story) — or, if all digits, by its id.

properties.label: Description (create/update)
properties.description: Plain text or Jira wiki markup. This connector speaks Jira's v2 API, so a description is a string rather than a document tree.

properties.label: Transition (transition)
properties.description: The workflow step by the name Jira shows on the button; its id is resolved first, so the model is not tied to one workflow configuration.

properties.label: Comment (comment/transition)
properties.description: Required for Add comment; on a Transition it is optional and is posted in the same call as the move.

properties.label: Assignee (assign)
properties.description: An accountId on Jira Cloud, a username on Data Center. Which one is decided by the connector's credential, not by this value.

properties.label: JQL (search)
properties.description: The query, written exactly as in Jira's own search box. It must restrict what it matches: Jira Cloud refuses an unbounded query, so one that only sorts is answered with an HTTP 400 rather than with every issue.

properties.label: Maximum issues (search)
properties.description: Caps what may reach the result variable; the connector pages up to it. Empty uses 50, 0 reads every match.

properties.label: Result variable (create/read/comment/search)
properties.description: Receives what Jira returned. Update, transition and assign answer with no content, and the compiler refuses a result variable on them.
